stories.headline: Fossils found in the 1970s turned out to be Denisovans
stories.summary: 20 fossils from Xujiayao in northern China were a puzzle for decades. Ancient proteins now show they're Denisovans, an extinct human group with a sloping forehead and a huge brow ridge.
stories.why: Denisovans were first known from just a finger bone in 2010. Now we can picture their faces.

stories.headline: A 9,000-year-old copper workshop was found in Türkiye
stories.summary: At Çayönü, archaeologists uncovered a 5 m² stone-paved work area where early farmers shaped green malachite and copper into beads. About 42 malachite and copper finds came out of it.
stories.why: It shows people there were working copper for about 2,000 years.

stories.headline: Solar power saved Spain €17 billion in 18 months
stories.summary: From January 2025 to June 2026, solar cut Spain's average wholesale power price to €60 a MWh, versus about €112 without it, a study by the national solar association found.
stories.why: Rooftop panels on homes and firms made up €2.8 billion of the savings, helping everyone's bill.

stories.headline: A giant sea bug in a museum for decades is a new species
stories.summary: Caught off Puerto Rico in the 1980s, this 32 cm giant isopod sat in a German collection under the wrong name. A CT scan revealed a comb of 15 bristles on its legs no relative has.
stories.why: Its makers say more new species may be hiding in museum drawers.

fun_fact: The new isopod's name honours Boríken, the Indigenous Taíno name for Puerto Rico.
